title: Stargate psychic spy program, 1972-1995

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, often tells of Stargate, which he calls a US government psychic spy program that ran from 1972 to 1995. It rested on "remote viewing", the claimed ability to describe distant places or hidden things using only the mind. A physicist named Hal Puthoff, who Michels says ran it and co-founded it with Russell Targ, says it started when viewers described super secret facilities and project titles locked in safes, and grew into a 20-year, 20 million dollar program. In some tellings it is a CIA program aimed at Russian nuclear bases and American hostages. Michels says it came up for funding every year and was shut down in 1995 under a man named Ed May, officially because it offered only offense and no defense, and that many later said it was not very effective. He adds that its files came out in 2017 through FOIA, a US law that lets anyone request government records. If true, it would mean the government spent decades seriously testing psychic abilities. Others repeat it on his show: a former intelligence officer, David Grusch, says Puthoff told him of many cases where the viewers' findings were confirmed by normal intelligence methods, a former Pentagon official, Lue Elizondo, calls Puthoff its godfather, and a Pentagon whistleblower, Matthew Brown, speaks of the problems with putting viewers on the official payroll.
